paper_metadata.title: Applying the Quantum Grover Algorithm to Improve the Efﬁciency of Growth Models

summary: The paper applies Grover's algorithm conceptually to parameter search in the Solow and Cobb-Douglas growth models, stating the standard quadratic speedup from O(N) classical search to O(\sqrt{N}) quantum search. It also gives the Grover iteration count as \u03c0/4 \u221a(2^n), but reports no hardware execution, qubit count, or empirical benchmark beyond the theoretical comparison.

experiments.description: Quantum Grover algorithm applied to optimize parameters in economic growth models (Solow and Cobb-Douglas) and analyze steady-state stability.

algorithm.variant: Grover search for optimal parameters in growth models

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Search over an unordered database of candidate parameter settings; the paper describes a binary oracle f:{0,1}^n -> {0,1} and Grover search over n-bit input registers, but does not specify a concrete qubit-to-variable mapping for the economic parameters.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Find x0 such that f(x0)=1; in the economic-model context, identify optimal parameters / steady-state conditions for the Solow and Cobb-Douglas models.

problem_instance.description: Parameter optimization and steady-state stability analysis for the Solow model and Cobb-Douglas model.

dataset_specification.description: Analytical economic growth models; no empirical dataset specified.

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Analytical derivation plus qualitative comparison to classical search; no repeated-run protocol or benchmark dataset reported.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical analytical/numerical methods for comparison; no specific solver named in the Grover experiment section.
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Derivation of Solow and Cobb-Douglas differential equations and steady-state conditions.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Interpretation of stability via derivative sign and comparison of search complexity.
